title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

x86/kvm: Don't consume async #PF flags on a kernel ...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

x86/kvm: Don't consume async #PF flags on a kernel #PF in NMI context

An async #PF "page not present" event arrives through the #PF vector,
and its reason sits in the per-CPU apf_reason.flags until
__kvm_handle_async_pf() reads and clears it. If an NMI arrives after
the event is injected and before the #PF handler reads the flags, and
the NMI handler itself takes a #PF, that fault reads and clears the
flags belonging to the #PF it interrupted. It then finds interrupts
disabled in the NMI context it interrupted, and panics:

  Kernel panic - not syncing: Host injected async #PF in interrupt
disabled region
  Call Trace:
   <NMI>
   panic+0x52/0x60
   __kvm_handle_async_pf+0xb0/0xb0
   exc_page_fault+0x71/0xb0
   asm_exc_page_fault+0x27/0x30
  RIP: 0010:__get_user_nocheck_8+0x6/0x20
   perf_callchain_user+0x147/0x1a0
   get_perf_callchain+0x12d/0x1c0
   ...
   perf_event_nmi_handler+0x26/0x50
   exc_nmi+0xe8/0x110
  RIP: 0010:asm_exc_page_fault+0x0/0x30
   </NMI>

The last RIP line shows the NMI landing on the first instruction of
the #PF entry. perf with user call chains takes such a fault: the
sampling NMI walks the user stack with __get_user(), which faults when
a saved frame pointer is not a valid user address or the walk runs off
the top of the stack. The same window exists when KVM, running as an
L1 hypervisor with DELIVERY_AS_PF_VMEXIT, reads the flags itself after
a #PF VM-exit.

The NMI entry code saves and restores CR2 for this nesting, but not the
async #PF reason. Andy Lutomirski described the race, with perf as the
example, when async #PF delivery was reworked in 2020 [1]. Saving and
clearing the flags across the NMI, next to CR2, was discussed there but
not merged.

Since that rework, Linux has stopped setting KVM_ASYNC_PF_SEND_ALWAYS,
so the host delivers "page not present" only for user mode faults and
a kernel-mode fault in NMI context (including kernel-mode #MC and #DB)
cannot be an async page fault.  In that case, return without touching
the flags so that the interrupted handler finds them intact.

Tested on v7.3-rc5 in a 4-vCPU, 2 GiB guest restored from a snapshot
whose memory is served on demand through userfaultfd, so that reading
it back takes async #PFs, while every thread samples hardware cycles
with user call chains and points its frame pointer at an unmapped page.
Without this patch the guest panicked as above in 3 of 3 runs. With it,
the guest survived 3 of 3 runs of 60 seconds, and the host counted
148,441 to 153,334 kvm_async_pf_not_present events in the first 20
seconds of each. On 6.18.50 the results were the same: the guest
panicked without the patch and survived with it.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: libsas: Fix SMP IO deadlock during HA resume
...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: libsas: Fix SMP IO deadlock during HA resume

smp_execute_task_sg() calls pm_runtime_get_sync() on the host before
issuing an SMP command. When that command is itself issued from the HA
resume path, the get_sync() deadlocks: it waits for the ongoing resume
(the device is RPM_RESUMING), while the resume is blocked in
sas_drain_work() waiting for that same SMP IO to complete.

The deadlock needs an expander-attached SATA disk. During
sas_resume_ha() -> sas_drain_work(), DISCE_RESUME -> sas_resume_sata()
-> ata_sas_port_resume() requests ATA_EH_RESET, and the hard reset for
such a disk is done via SMP PHY CONTROL (sas_ata_hard_reset() ->
sas_phy_reset() -> sas_smp_phy_control() ->
smp_execute_task_sg()). Direct-attached SATA resets through
lldd_control_phy() and SSP devices use TMFs, so neither hits this.

Replace the get_sync()/put_sync() pair with
pm_runtime_get_noresume()/pm_runtime_put(). smp_execute_task_sg() only
needs to hold off autosuspend while the SMP is in flight, and it must
not try to resume the host: a sync resume issued from the HA resume path
itself is what deadlocks, and by the time sas_resume_ha() runs, hw_init
has already reinitialized the hardware, so the device is accessible
without one.

The usage reference is still required. Discovery work normally runs
inside an event worker's PM reference, taken at sas_notify_port_event()
notify time and held until the handler has flushed the disco
queue. sas_rediscover_ex_phy() however requeues DISCE_REVALIDATE_DOMAIN
from within the revalidation worker itself, and flush_workqueue() does
not wait for work items queued during execution, so that chained
revalidation runs with no outer PM reference - without the
get_noresume(), its SMP could race autosuspend.

For the BSG path, sas_smp_handler() is the only caller which may find
the host autosuspended: expander SMP requests do not go through any SCSI
device request queue, so nothing else in that path holds the host
awake. Resume it there with pm_runtime_resume_and_get() and check the
result.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2/dlm: Protect the recovery list during debugfs...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2/dlm: Protect the recovery list during debugfs reads

Recovery participant records must remain alive while debug_state_print()
walks reco.node_data and formats their fields. The formatter holds
dlm->spinlock, but the recovery participant list is protected by
dlm_reco_state_lock. In particular, dlm_destroy_recovery_area() detaches
the list under dlm_reco_state_lock and frees the detached records after
releasing it. A concurrent debugfs open can therefore read freed memory.

Protect the participant traversal and field reads in debug_state_print()
with dlm_reco_state_lock, matching the existing list writers. This also
serializes the traversal against list_add_tail() during recovery-area
initialization. Make the existing lock available to the debug code
through dlmcommon.h; the lock remains internal to the OCFS2 DLM module.

Release dlm->spinlock after formatting the other domain state and before
acquiring dlm_reco_state_lock, so the debug reader does not nest the two
locks. Leave recovery list insertion, detachment and freeing unchanged.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/vc4: hdmi: Move packet RAM enable to PM runtime...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/vc4: hdmi: Move packet RAM enable to PM runtime

Audio can be triggered by the HPD handler and start up before video has
been restored, calling vc4_hdmi_write_infoframe() for the audio infoframe.
vc4_hdmi_write_infoframe() needs Packet RAM to be on to store the
infoframe, however, if the video hasn't been enabled,
vc4_hdmi_encoder_post_crtc_enable() hasn't been called and therefore, the
Packet RAM can be disabled by the time vc4_hdmi_write_infoframe() executes,
causing the following splat:

[  201.570266] ------------[ cut here ]------------
[  201.570293] Packet RAM has to be on to store the packet.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

power: supply: core: prevent unregistering a power ...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

power: supply: core: prevent unregistering a power supply while a callback runs

Once a power supply is registered, its callbacks can immediately start
firing from other contexts, such as external_power_changed() triggered by
the TCPM stack. If a power supply is unregistered while the callback is
still running, the driver data can already be freed when the callback
tries to access it, leading to a use-after-free.

This happens e.g. when the hardware bus carrying the power supply device
malfunctions (e.g. I2C is hogged down by another malfunctioning device)
immediately after the power supply is registered, and thus the core is
still processing the callbacks which were queued up when the driver
starts the removal, leading in some cases to a kernel crash, e.g.:

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: p54: validate firmware record lengths

The p5...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: p54: validate firmware record lengths

The p54 firmware parser accesses component ID and component version
records without checking that their lengths cover the fields being read.
A malformed record can therefore make the parser read past the record.

Validate the component ID and component version record lengths before
accessing their data. The descriptor record is also checked against the
shortest descriptor length found in the supported firmware images.

Reject descriptor values that underflow the RX offset or produce an empty
RX range before updating the driver state.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/i915/dmc: Harden DMC firmware payload parsing

...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/i915/dmc: Harden DMC firmware payload parsing

Validate the conversion of the DMC firmware size from dwords to bytes
using check_mul_overflow() before calculating the firmware payload size.

Reject zero-length payloads and zero MMIO counts in the DMC firmware
header so malformed firmware is caught early. Also set dmc_fw_size only
after the payload allocation succeeds.

(cherry picked from commit efde6601a1f1daedfe3dcc2816c934ddb44e3eef)

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/i915/dmc: Add sanity check for DMC load address...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/i915/dmc: Add sanity check for DMC load address

For DMC firmware header version 3, the firmware load address is stored
in dmc_info->start_mmioaddr and later used by dmc_load_program().

Unlike the MMIO address table, the firmware load address is not
validated. Add a sanity check to ensure it is within the valid range.

BSpec: 69671, 68378
(cherry picked from commit 5e47ee5c76ca9becde8df4ad5202845b7ffcbc4c)

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tcp: fix use-after-free in do_tcp_getsockopt(TCP_CC...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tcp: fix use-after-free in do_tcp_getsockopt(TCP_CC_INFO)

do_tcp_getsockopt() reads icsk->icsk_ca_ops and dereferences the
get_info function pointer without rcu_read_lock(). With BPF struct_ops
congestion control, ca_ops can point to dynamically allocated memory
that is freed concurrently, resulting in a use-after-free when the
kernel dereferences or calls through the stale pointer.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in do_tcp_getsockopt+0x2037/0x23e0
  Read of size 8 at addr ffff888013701258 by task exploit/149
   do_tcp_getsockopt+0x2037/0x23e0 (net/ipv4/tcp.c:4564)
   tcp_getsockopt+0x91/0xf0
   __sys_getsockopt+0xf7/0x170

Fix this by wrapping the ca_ops load and get_info call within
rcu_read_lock()/rcu_read_unlock(), and using READ_ONCE() to load
the icsk_ca_ops pointer.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tcp: fix use-after-free in do_tcp_getsockopt(TCP_CO...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tcp: fix use-after-free in do_tcp_getsockopt(TCP_CONGESTION)

do_tcp_getsockopt() reads icsk->icsk_ca_ops->name without holding
rcu_read_lock(). Since commit 0baf26b0fcd7 ("bpf: tcp: Support
tcp_congestion_ops in bpf"), icsk_ca_ops can point to dynamically
allocated BPF struct_ops memory that may be freed concurrently via
setsockopt(TCP_CONGESTION), leading to a use-after-free.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in _copy_to_user+0x37/0x60
  Read of size 16 at addr ffff888013505260 by task exploit/149
   _copy_to_user+0x37/0x60
   do_tcp_getsockopt+0x158a/0x2460 (net/ipv4/tcp.c:4585)
   tcp_getsockopt+0x91/0xf0
   __sys_getsockopt+0xf7/0x170

Fix this by holding rcu_read_lock() around the ca_ops->name access,
using READ_ONCE() to load icsk_ca_ops, and copying the name to a
stack buffer before releasing the lock. Also annotate the relevant
icsk_ca_ops stores with WRITE_ONCE() to fix the accompanying KCSAN
data-race issue.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: ti: icssm-prueth: Move setting of netops to fi...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: ti: icssm-prueth: Move setting of netops to fix crash

icssm_prueth_netdev_init() calls of_phy_get_and_connect() before
ndev->netdev_ops is assigned. phy_attach_direct() ->
phy_link_topo_add_phy() reads dev->netdev_ops through
netdev_need_ops_lock() since the commit in question, so probing crashes
with a NULL pointer dereference when CONFIG_NET_SHAPER is enabled.

Assign netdev_ops before the PHY attach, as was done for emac in commit
7c9f391ec89c ("net: emac: move setting of netops to fix crash").

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ntfs: take invalidate_lock in ntfs_setattr_size()

...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ntfs: take invalidate_lock in ntfs_setattr_size()

ntfs_setattr_size() updates i_size and resizes the on-disk attribute
without holding mapping->invalidate_lock.  Page faults take the lock
shared, so a fault racing the resize can resolve a VCN against the
transient runlist state of ntfs_non_resident_attr_expand() and fail
with a spurious SIGBUS, and can interleave with the size-change
epilogue (truncate_pagecache(), i_size_write(),
pagecache_isize_extended()).

Take invalidate_lock exclusively around the whole resize after
inode_dio_wait(), matching the fallocate path and other filesystems
such as xfs, which wraps truncate in its mmaplock (= invalidate_lock).

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mac802154: fix data race and NULL deref on local->a...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mac802154: fix data race and NULL deref on local->assoc_dev

local->assoc_dev is shared between the association path and the
association-response worker without common synchronization.

mac802154_perform_association() stores the coordinator pointer and waits
for a response. Its timeout and error paths clear the pointer and return
to mac802154_associate(), which may then free the coordinator object.
Meanwhile, mac802154_rx_mac_cmd_worker() may observe the associating bit
and enter mac802154_process_association_resp(), which dereferences
assoc_dev.

The worker's bit test and the handler's pointer dereference are not
atomic with respect to cleanup. Cleanup can clear assoc_dev between them,
causing a NULL dereference, or free the coordinator while the response
handler still uses the pointer.

The recorded result is exposed to the same window. assoc_status and
assoc_addr are written by the handler but read by the association path
while the associating bit is still set, so a second response for the same
request - a malicious one, for instance - can replace them between those
reads and leave the caller with an incoherent status and address pair.

The response handler only needs the coordinator extended address.
Replace assoc_dev with a cached address, removing the pointer lifetime
dependency. Protect the cached address and the associating bit with a
dedicated spinlock. A READ_ONCE()/WRITE_ONCE() pair would not guarantee
an atomic __le64 access on all 32-bit architectures.

wpan_dev->association_lock cannot be reused here: nl802154_associate()
holds it across rdev_associate(), hence for the whole of
mac802154_perform_association() including the wait for the response.
A response handler taking that lock would only get it once the
association has already given up.

Reset the completion, publish the cached address, and set the associating
bit while holding the lock. The response handler takes the lock, rechecks
the bit and the cached address, records the response, clears the bit, and
only then completes the waiter. Thus cleanup cannot pass the handler
between its state check and completion, and the cached 64-bit value
cannot tear.

The handler clears the bit before completing, not the woken waiter:
otherwise complete() is issued under the lock and a second (e.g.
malicious) response can reacquire it before the waiter and replace the
result. So a wait that returns success implies the bit is already clear,
and the success and negative-response paths return directly. The
transmit-error and timeout paths still clear it under assoc_lock, which
serializes any racing response against the cleanup while the call returns
the error it already selected. Both paths snapshot assoc_status and
assoc_addr under the same lock.

Both users run in process context, so a plain spinlock is sufficient.
The lock is not held while waiting for the completion.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/xe: Don't transfer shrinker pages for pinned bo...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/xe: Don't transfer shrinker pages for pinned bos on purgeable state change

Pinned bos have their pages removed from the shrinker's shrinkable /
purgeable counts on pin, and added back on unpin according to the
bo's purgeable state at that time.

However, xe_bo_set_purgeable_shrinker() unconditionally transfers
pages between the shrinkable and purgeable counts. If the purgeable
state of a pinned bo changes, for example by userspace madvising
DONTNEED on a VMA of a bo that is also pinned as a scanout buffer,
this underflows one count and, after unpin, leaves the other one
permanently inflated.

Only update the purgeable flag for pinned bos, and leave the page
accounting to unpin.

(cherry picked from commit afe6bc012034123fd838328668e609bf57e46bd3)

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/exec: don't immediately add prelocked obj to ar...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/exec: don't immediately add prelocked obj to array of locked objs

When a contention is detected the drm_exec object grabs a reference to
the contended object, unlocks all other objects and pre-locks the
contended one before anything else.

The problem is that it is possible that this pre-locked object was about
to be destroyed and drm_exec is now holding the last reference to it.

So we never actually see this pre-locked object again to be explicitly
locked and so also never reserve a slot for a dma_fence object on it.

Should the driver now use drm_exec_for_each_locked_object() to add a new
fence to all locked objects we eventually see a warning or even a
BUG_ON() to prevent random memory corruption.

Fix this by keeping the prelocked object out of the array of locked objs
until it was explicitly mentioned by the driver again.

If the prelocked object is never mentioned again by the driver
just unlock and drop the reference at the end of the locking loop.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: fix GEM object leak on ENOMEM in userpt...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: fix GEM object leak on ENOMEM in userptr ioctl

When amdgpu_hmm_range_alloc() fails amdgpu_gem_userptr_ioctl() returns
-ENOMEM right away and skips the cleanup every other error path goes
through. The GEM object, the bo->parent reference on the VM root and the
MMU notifier registration are all left behind.

Use release_object here, not user_pages_done, range is still NULL at
this point.

(cherry picked from commit bbe739e407a542073ec1a7872b14843566b4919e)

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: bsg: Pass reply_len to bsg_setup_queue() to f...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: bsg: Pass reply_len to bsg_setup_queue() to fit UFS ARPMB replies

bsg-lib allocates a 96-byte (SCSI_SENSE_BUFFERSIZE) reply buffer per
job, but struct ufs_rpmb_reply is 104 bytes: a 40-byte struct
ufs_bsg_reply followed by a 64-byte EHS. When an Advanced RPMB command
returns an EHS, ufshcd_advanced_rpmb_req_handler() copies it right after
the 40-byte header and writes 8 bytes past the end of the buffer.

Let each BSG transport pass its reply buffer size to bsg_setup_queue()
and have ufs_bsg request sizeof(struct ufs_rpmb_reply), so the full
reply reaches user space. Other transports keep SCSI_SENSE_BUFFERSIZE.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ring-buffer: Do not show buffer_meta for CPUs witho...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ring-buffer: Do not show buffer_meta for CPUs without a buffer

The per_cpu/cpuN/buffer_meta files are created for every possible CPU,
but buffer->buffers[cpu] is only allocated once that CPU comes online.
Reading the file of a CPU that never came online dereferences a NULL
cpu_buffer in rbm_start().

Fail the open with -ENODEV when the CPU has no buffer, as the other
per CPU ring buffer interfaces do.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: rds: fix uninitialized trans dereference in CM...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: rds: fix uninitialized trans dereference in CM event handler

rds_rdma_cm_event_handler_cmn() assigns trans only when the RDMA
device is an InfiniBand CA (RDMA_NODE_IB_CA).  On any other device
type, e.g. an iWARP RNIC such as siw, trans stays uninitialized, but
the event switch dereferences it: unconditionally in the
RDMA_CM_EVENT_CONNECT_REQUEST case via trans->cm_handle_connect(),
and (with a connection context) in the ROUTE_RESOLVED and
ESTABLISHED cases.

An RDS listener on an iWARP device therefore crashes the kernel as
soon as a connect request arrives: with CONFIG_INIT_STACK_ALL_ZERO
the wild load becomes a NULL dereference at offset 0xa0
(&trans->cm_handle_connect) in the iw_cm_wq workqueue.

GCC masks the bug in default builds by folding the uninitialized
load into &rds_ib_transport; Clang-built kernels take the real
uninitialized path and oops.

The active side can land on a non-IB device too: the id that
rds_ib_conn_path_connect() creates is not restricted to a node type,
so rdma_resolve_addr() binds it to whichever device serves the local
address, and an iWARP RNIC on the same netdev qualifies.  The crash
there is different: resolving a route on an iWARP id never fills in
cm_id->route.path_rec, and the ROUTE_RESOLVED case writes
path_rec[0].sl before it calls into the transport.

The iWARP transport was dropped long ago and IB is the only
transport left, so make that explicit: initialize trans to
&rds_ib_transport at declaration, drop the conditional assignment,
reject a connect request that arrives on a non-IB device, and drop a
connection whose address resolved to one instead of resolving a
route on it.  The rejection is limited to RDMA_CM_EVENT_CONNECT_REQUEST
on purpose: a non-zero return from the handler makes rdma_cm destroy
the id the event was delivered on, which is right for the request's
freshly created id but would free a connection id that RDS still owns
for any other event.  On the active side the id stays ic->i_cm_id and
the connection's shutdown destroys it, so that case returns 0.

[achender: reject only on RDMA_CM_EVENT_CONNECT_REQUEST instead of
 bailing out for every event on a non-IB device, so that rdma_cm does
 not destroy connection ids RDS still tracks; drop a connection whose
 address resolved to a non-IB device before a route is resolved on it;
 changelog adjusted]

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ntfs3: free the sbi after a grace period

If the "n...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ntfs3: free the sbi after a grace period

If the "nocase" mount option ntfs3 uses custom hash and dentry compare
functions. Both access ntfs3 superblock private information in rcu
pathwalk. ntfs_put_super() and ntfs3_kill_sb() drop the info without any
rcu delay. A lookup that's still inside the filesystem when the last
reference to the mount is dropped causes a UAF. With a pathwalk held up
in ntfs_d_hash() while the last reference to the mount goes away:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in ntfs_nls_to_utf16+0x752/0x940
  Read of size 8 at addr ff1100010453c850 by task walker/99
  Call Trace:
   <TASK>
   ntfs_nls_to_utf16+0x752/0x940
   ntfs_d_hash+0x22b/0x500
   link_path_walk+0x11ad/0x1d30
   path_lookupat+0x63/0xb00
   filename_lookup+0x1f1/0x5b0
   vfs_statx+0xd7/0x3b0
  [...]
  Allocated by task 95:
   __kmalloc_cache_noprof+0x249/0x560
   ntfs_init_fs_context+0x2db/0x5a0
   alloc_fs_context+0x52e/0xc70
  [...]
  Freed by task 98:
   kfree+0x1db/0x5b0
   deactivate_locked_super+0x9c/0xf0
   cleanup_mnt+0x9f/0x130
   task_work_run+0x131/0x250

The bug is currently masked by the grace period in namespace_unlock()
for umount(2). Keep the necessary information until the filesystem
private info is freed and free it with an rcu delay.

ntfs3_free_sbi() now runs from an rcu callback and drops the upcase
table via ntfs_put_shared(). So switch s_shared_lock over to
spin_lock_bh(). Otherwise the callback can deadlock against a task
holding the lock on the same cpu.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

perf: Fix perf_pmu_migrate_context() leaving events...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

perf: Fix perf_pmu_migrate_context() leaving events behind

__perf_pmu_remove() walks the group leaders of a CPU and PMU with
perf_event_groups_for_cpu_pmu(), removing each one as it goes.
perf_remove_from_context() takes the leader out of the groups rbtree,
after which rb_next() on that node returns NULL, prematurely ending the
walk. Other groups stay behind in the source context.

On CPU hotplug, they are then torn down with the dying CPU. They keep
running until teardown, while the PMU's interrupt and migrated events
are on a new CPU, which drivers rely on never happening.

Walk ctx->event_list instead and pick out the PMU's events by their
pmu_ctx.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

calipso: keep BIG TCP payload_len in calipso_skbuff...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

calipso: keep BIG TCP payload_len in calipso_skbuff_setattr()

calipso_skbuff_setattr() adjusts payload_len by the length of the
option it inserts or resizes:

	payload = ntohs(ip6_hdr->payload_len);
	ip6_hdr->payload_len = htons(payload + len_delta);

GRO can build BIG TCP packets larger than IPV6_MAXPLEN, and stores
payload_len == 0 for them; ipv6_payload_len() then falls back to
skb->len.  For such a packet forwarded to a destination mapped to
CALIPSO, the code above writes len_delta (or 65536 + len_delta when
shrinking) into payload_len, and ipv6_payload_len() no longer falls
back to skb->len.  nf_tables, conntrack and sch_cake rely on it.

The same arithmetic also wraps when a packet grows past IPV6_MAXPLEN,
and a BIG TCP packet that shrinks below IPV6_MAXPLEN should get its
real length back.

Set payload_len from the skb length with ipv6_set_payload_len(), which
stores 0 above IPV6_MAXPLEN and the real length otherwise, as
ipv6_gro_complete() does.  The network header was just reset to
skb->data, so skb->len - sizeof(*ip6_hdr) is the payload length.

Tested on one kernel (arm64, QEMU) with SELinux permissive, a minimal
mdp-generated policy (network_peer_controls=1), "netlabelctl calipso
add pass doi:16" and a NetLabel mapping of fd00:2::/64 to CALIPSO
DOI 16.  calipso_skbuff_setattr() was called through
netlbl_skbuff_setattr() from a test-only debugfs hook (not part of
this patch) adding a level-only label; payload_len after the call:

  case                         before fix   after fix   real length
  1000, unlabeled                    1016        1016          1016
  70000 GSO, payload_len 0             16           0         70016
  65530 GSO, grows past MAXPLEN        10           0         65546
  65540 GSO with a 24 byte hop
  header, shrinks below MAXPLEN     65528       65532         65532
  1000 with a 24 byte hop header      992         992           992

(0 means ipv6_payload_len() returns the real length.)  On the forward
path, with a client injecting unlabeled UDP through a router to a
server, the router adds the CALIPSO option and the server delivers all
datagrams (Udp6InDatagrams 5, Ip6InTruncatedPkts 0) with this patch.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sched/core: Call wakeup_preempt() for queued tasks ...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sched/core: Call wakeup_preempt() for queued tasks during class change

Paul reported recent RCU changes exposed a lost resched where CPU idles
with a rcutorture thread waiting while being completely runnable.

Dumping the rq state at the time of idling with runnable tasks showed
the following:

  rq->next_class = &fair_sched_class
  rq->nr_running = 1
  rq->cfs.h_nr_queued = 0
  rq->rt.rt_nr_running = 1

Although the waiting task was an RT task, "rq->next_class" did not point
to rt_sched_class and was stuck at the lower priority fair_sched_class.

Inspecting sched_change_end() revealed the following race with
__sched_setscheduler() for queued, but non-running tasks:

    CPU0                                   CPU1
    ====                                   ====

  __schedule()

    /*
     * rq->donor is a fair task that blocks.
     * rq->next_class = &fair_sched_class
     */

    rq_lock(rq0)

    pick_next_task()
      /* nr_running = 0 */
      pick_task_fair()
        sched_balance_newidle()
          raw_spin_rq_unlock(rq0)
                                    rq_lock(rq0)

                                    activate_task(rq0, p)
                                      /* p is a fair task */
                                      rq0->nr_running++;
                                      rq0->cfs.h_nr_queued++;
                                      wakeup_preempt(rq, p)
                                        rq->next_class = &fair_sched_class
                                        resched_curr()

                                    rq_unlock(rq0)

                                    __sched_setscheduler(p)
                                      /* p is moved to SCHED_RR */
                                      task_rq_lock(p)
                                      sched_change_begin()

				      rq0->cfs.h_nr_queued--;
				      rq0->rt.rt_nr_running++;

                                      sched_change_end()
                                        /*
                                         * p->on_rq = 1 (ctx->queued)
                                         * but p is not rq->donor
                                         * (!ctx->running) hence
                                         * resched_curr() is and
                                         * rq->next_class upgrade is
                                         * skipped.
                                         */

                                       task_rq_unlock()

          raw_spin_rq_lock(rq0)

          /*
           * rq->nr_running = 1
           * rq->cfs.h_nr_queued = 0
           * rq->rt.rt_nr_running = 1
           * rq->next_class = &fair_sched_class
           */

           if (rq->cfs.h_nr_queued && ...)
             /* Above is false */

           if (rq_modified_above(this_rq, &fair_sched_class))
             /* Also false since rq->next_class is still fair */

      /*
       * sched_balance_newidle() is considered to
       * have failed to pull any fair tasks and no
       * other wakeups were detected.
       */
       return NULL; /* pick_task_fair() */

    pick_task_idle()
      return rq->idle;

    next = rq->idle;

    /* Preemption indicators are lost */
    clear_tsk_need_resched(prev);
    clear_preempt_need_resched();

    rq->curr = rq->idle;

  !!! rq->idle switches in with rq->running == 1 but !need_resched() !!!

In simple words, enqueue, followed by a class change of the newly queued
task goes unnoticed in rq->next_class indicator and
sched_balance_newidle() sees no fair task, nor any higher priority task
enqueued.

The above sequence will lead to CPU idling with a runnable task on the
CPU.

Call wakeup_preempt() for ctx->queued cases in sched_change_end() to
re-evaluate rq->next_class after class change (ENQUEUE_CLASS) and set
the NEED_RESCHED indicator accordingly.

Newidle balance will correctly see an enqueue of a higher priority
t
---truncated---

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: target: iscsi: Fix race in discovery auth upd...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: target: iscsi: Fix race in discovery auth updates

Separate configfs opens can concurrently update the discovery AuthMethod
parameter. Both callers may free the same value in
iscsi_update_param_value(), causing a double-free.

Protect the lookup and replacement with the discovery TPG access lock,
as used by the other TPG configfs parameter updates.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: target: Disable interrupts while holding dela...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: target: Disable interrupts while holding delayed_cmd_lock

target_do_delayed_work() takes dev->delayed_cmd_lock with a plain
spin_lock(). It runs from system_percpu_wq, so interrupts stay enabled
while the lock is held. Every other acquisition of that lock uses
spin_lock_irqsave(): target_handle_task_attr() and
transport_complete_ordered_sync() in target_core_transport.c, and
target_non_ordered_release() in target_core_device.c.

That was safe while every caller of transport_complete_task_attr() ran
in process context: target_complete_ok_work() from target_completion_wq,
transport_complete_qf() from dev->qf_work_queue, and
transport_generic_request_failure() from the submit and execute paths.

Since commit 06933066d88a ("scsi: target: Add support for completing
commands from backend context") that is no longer true. With
complete_type=1 on a fabric that sets direct_compl_supp,
target_complete() runs target_complete_ok_work() inline in the backend's
completion context, which target_complete_cmd_with_sense() documents as
"May be called from interrupt context". For iblock that is the bio
end_io.

target_complete_ok_work() starts with transport_complete_task_attr(),
which takes delayed_cmd_lock in two ways:

 - Every ORDERED command is put on dev->delayed_cmd_list by
   target_handle_task_attr() and dispatched from there by
   target_do_delayed_work(), which marks it SCF_TASK_ORDERED_SYNC.  Its
   completion therefore goes through transport_complete_ordered_sync().

 - A SIMPLE command that completes while an ORDERED command is pending
   drops the last reference to the killed dev->non_ordered, and
   percpu_ref_put() then runs target_non_ordered_release() in the
   completing context.

Both take the lock and, if commands are waiting, call
schedule_work(&dev->delayed_cmd_work), which queues on system_percpu_wq,
i.e. on the CPU that took the completion. Further completions for the
same queue are typically delivered there too, so one arriving while the
work holds the lock spins on it forever.

Reaching this needs complete_type=1, which is not the default
(vhost-scsi, the only fabric with direct_compl_supp, defaults to
TARGET_QUEUE_COMPL), a backend whose I/O completes from interrupt
context, and ORDERED commands from the initiator. Linux virtio_scsi
guests send only VIRTIO_SCSI_S_SIMPLE and never take the ordered path;
any guest that uses the ORDERED task attribute, which vhost-scsi
accepts, does.

target_do_delayed_work() is a work item and always runs in process
context, so spin_lock_irq() is sufficient.

Found by inspection; no runtime report. A single ORDERED command goes
through both acquisitions, so with CONFIG_PROVE_LOCKING the first one
completed through direct completion should produce an inconsistent lock
state report on delayed_cmd_lock (hardirq or softirq, depending on where
the backend completes).

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netlink: reset skb headers before unicast and multi...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netlink: reset skb headers before unicast and multicast filtering

Socket filters can use SKF_NET_OFF and SKF_LL_OFF to read relative to
an skb's network and MAC headers. Netlink producers may reserve
headroom without resetting those headers, allowing a receiving socket's
filter to read data before the initialized message.

For example, IWPM HELLO replies are allocated with dev_alloc_skb(),
which reserves NET_SKB_PAD bytes. An unprivileged NETLINK_RDMA user can
attach a classic socket filter and disclose this headroom through the
length of the delivered reply. The resets in netlink_dump() do not help
because IWPM sends a separately allocated skb through netlink_unicast().

Reset both headers before running the receiver's filter in unicast and
broadcast delivery, as is already done for dump skbs. This also covers
other netlink producers that reserve headroom without changing their
allocation or message-building code.

title: ServiceNow has remediated an information disclosure vulnerability that was identified in the ServiceNow AI Platform. Thi...
description:
ServiceNow has remediated an information disclosure vulnerability that was identified in the ServiceNow AI Platform. This vulnerability could cause a user's plaintext password to be persisted in a system table, potentially exposing that password to a user who otherwise would not be entitled to view it.





ServiceNow remediated the vulnerability through security updates that address the unintended persistence of plaintext credentials. We are not currently aware of malicious exploitation against ServiceNow instances. We recommend customers promptly apply appropriate updates or upgrade to a patched release if they have not already done so.

title: In Teltonika Networks RUTOS devices running versions from 7.22 through 7.24.2 and TSWOS devices running versions 1.9 thr...
description:
In Teltonika Networks RUTOS devices running versions from 7.22 through 7.24.2 and TSWOS devices running versions 1.9 through 1.10, a vulnerability exists whereby an unauthenticated user can directly call LUA functions, bypassing validations that might be called under normal API requests. Due to those requests not following proper flows, this could lead to OS command execution.



This issue affects RUT: from 7.22 through 7.24.2; RUTX: from 7.22 through 7.24.2; RUTM: from 7.22 through 7.24.2; RUTC: from 7.22 through 7.24.2; ATRM: from 7.22 through 7.24.2; TAP: from 7.22 through 7.24.2; CAP: from 7.22 through 7.24.2; OXA: from 7.22 through 7.24.2; DAP: from 7.22 through 7.24.2; TRB: from 7.22 through 7.24.2; OTD: from 7.22 through 7.24.2; EBG: from 7.22 through 7.24.2; SWM: from 1.9 through 1.10; TSW: from 1.9 through 1.10.

title: An information disclosure vulnerability in the Forocoches comments editor that allows an attacker to obtain unauthorised...
description: An information disclosure vulnerability in the Forocoches comments editor that allows an attacker to obtain unauthorised user information by inserting an image containing a malicious external URL into a comment. When a victim views the discussion thread, their browser automatically sends an HTTP/HTTPS request to the server controlled by the attacker, who can then collect information such as the source IP address, the User-Agent header, the date and time of access, and other metadata derived from the request, thereby compromising the user’s privacy.

title: A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the chart feature of SharePoint Manager Plus (SPMP) due to i...
description: A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the chart feature of SharePoint Manager Plus (SPMP) due to improper sanitization and HTML encoding of user-controlled data. An attacker can inject malicious HTML or JavaScript into attributes used to generate charts, including users' full names, site names, or group names. The injected content is stored and subsequently executed in the context of other users' browsers when the affected charts are rendered. This vulnerability was fixed in client application build 4508.

title: Acceptance of Extraneous Untrusted Data With Trusted Data vulnerability in the Sign in with Apple strategy in pow-auth A...
description:
Acceptance of Extraneous Untrusted Data With Trusted Data vulnerability in the Sign in with Apple strategy in pow-auth Assent allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to impersonate another user via the user parameter of the authorization callback.

Apple posts the user's name to the callback endpoint in a user form parameter that the browser submits and the client controls. Assent.Strategy.Apple.callback/2 in lib/assent/strategies/apple.ex decodes that parameter, and fetch_user/2 merges it over the claims of the verified ID token, so the unverified map wins. An attacker who completes a Sign in with Apple login with their own Apple ID and edits the user parameter can replace sub, email, and any other claim. Applications that look up, link, or authorize accounts by the returned subject or email then act on the attacker's values.

This issue affects assent: from 0.1.25 before 0.3.2.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

keys/trusted_keys: return immediately after TPM uns...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

keys/trusted_keys: return immediately after TPM unseal failure

trusted_tpm_unseal() proceeds to pcrlock() when the TPM unseal operation
fails. If pcrlock() succeeds, its return value overwrites the unseal error,
causing key instantiation to succeed.

Return immediately when unseal fails to preserve the original error.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/io-wq: don't lose the signal that ends wor...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/io-wq: don't lose the signal that ends work

When a thread exits, only its tracked requests are cancelled. Then its
io-wq is torn down. io_wq_exit_workers() signals every worker, to get it
out of an interruptible sleep, and waits for all of them to exit. Before
they do, they go through the work that is left. Unbounded work is
cancelled. Bounded work is run, as it is expected to end by itself.

Not all of it does. An open has no file yet, so it counts as bounded, and
the open of a FIFO waits for the other end. That is what the signal is for.
But the workers are signalled once, and a worker that hasn't started the
work by then loses the signal:

  io_wq_exit_workers()               io_worker_handle_work()
    io_wq_worker_wake()
      set TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL
                                       io_assign_current_work()
                                         io_run_task_work()
                                           clear TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL
                                       io_wq_submit_work()
                                         fifo_open()
                                           wait_for_partner()
    wait_for_completion_timeout()

The thread never gets out of do_exit():

  IORING_OP_OPENAT of a FIFO without a writer, IOSQE_ASYNC
  exit of the thread that has submitted it

hangs in more than 9 of 10 attempts (4 CPUs, KVM), until the process is
killed.

Set TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL for bounded work that is started with IO_WQ_BIT_EXIT
set. The bit is set before the workers are signalled, and it is tested
after the flag has been cleared, with clear_notify_signal() providing the
barrier. So either the flag stays, or the bit is seen.

Work that is started while the io-wq exits is treated like work that is
being run at that time: it isn't interrupted unless it waits
interruptibly.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/cmd: don't leave list poison in ->hash_nod...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/cmd: don't leave list poison in ->hash_node

io_uring_cmd_del_cancelable() uses hlist_del() to take a command off
->cancelable_uring_cmd, which leaves LIST_POISON1/2 behind in
->hash_node. Requests are recycled through the request cache without
being reinitialised, and not every user of ->hash_node sets it up before
it is used:

If a vectored futex wait is woken while futex_wait_multiple_setup() is
still queueing the futexes, io_futexv_wait() doesn't add the request to
->futex_list, and leaves the completion to the task_work queued by the
wake up. io_futexv_complete() ends in __io_futex_complete(), whose
hlist_del_init() is fine for a request that is unhashed, which is how all
other users of the node leave it. If the request was a cancelable
uring_cmd in its previous life, e.g. a ublk FETCH_REQ, it writes through
LIST_POISON2:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
  KASAN: maybe wild-memory-access in range [0xdead000000000120-...]
  RIP: 0010:io_futexv_complete+0x219/0x420
  Call Trace:
   tctx_task_work_run+0x804/0x950
   tctx_task_work+0x71/0xa0
   task_work_run+0x118/0x200

Leave the node unhashed.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

printk: Postpone kthread startup

There have been v...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

printk: Postpone kthread startup

There have been various bug reports related to SMP systems hanging
on boot. The reports vary but seem to have some overlap with regard
to missed IPI's during SMP setup. The reports also show that
reverting NBCON console usage allows the bugs to disappear.

The NBCON kthreads for console printing are started very early
during boot using early_initcall(). Since these kthreads are
asynchronously enabling/disabling interrupts during early boot, they
may be interfering with early SMP setup on some hardware platforms.

Starting the console printing kthreads later has shown to avoid the
hanging on systems that could previously reproduce the issue.

Postpone kthread starting until after all arch initcalls have
completed.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

pid_namespace: prevent TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL from inter...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

pid_namespace: prevent TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL from interrupting the reaper

Since commit 7fea700e04bd ("zap_pid_ns_processes: clear
TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL along with TIF_SIGPENDING") zap_pid_ns_processes()
clears TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL before every kernel_wait4() call. Otherwise
kernel_wait4() doesn't sleep and returns -ERESTARTSYS if
signal_pending() is true and the reaper busy-waits.

But clearing TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL doesn't fix it. It can get raised again.
For example, klp_send_signals() sets it raw against any task that hasn't
transitioned yet. And it keeps sending it until the livepatch finishes.

The sleep loop waiting for pid_allocated to drop has the same problem
and it doesn't even clear anything. So a schedule() in
TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE returns immediately.

Use a no_notify_signal guard. signal_pending() will ignore
TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL and the pid namespace reaper sleeps until a child
exits or free_pid() wakes it.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring: don't flood a cancelling task with task_w...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring: don't flood a cancelling task with task_work

io_ring_exit_work() asks each task which has used the ring to remove its
tctx node, by task_work, and repeats that until the list is empty.
io_tctx_exit_cb() doesn't touch the node while the task is in
io_uring_cancel_generic(), which removes all the nodes at its end. So the
work item queues the callback again as soon as it has completed, for
nothing.

That is more than a waste of time. task_work_run() only returns when it
finds the list empty. If the rings are released from inside the
cancellation, because requests of other rings held the last references to
their files, up to 64 work items keep sending callbacks to the one task
which is running them. It never finds the list empty, never gets back to
the cancellation, the nodes stay, and so it goes on: a task with 60 pairs
of rings which poll each other ran 280000 callbacks in 5 seconds, 20
seconds after exit_group(). It ends when all the senders happen to be late
at the same time. Until then the task keeps a CPU and the work items busy.

An exiting task can't be killed meanwhile. execve() cancels the requests in
the same way, so a live task can get stuck there as well, for minutes. If
it takes more than five, the work items run into the
WARN_ON_ONCE(time_after(jiffies, timeout)) of io_ring_exit_work(). No
privilege is needed for any of this.

If the callback has met a task in cancellation, wait a little before it is
sent again. Nobody has to wake the work item up for that: either the node
is gone by then, or it is the turn of the next round.

title: A use of uninitialized memory vulnerability in the pybddisasm Python bindings affects nd_to_text. If the underlying text...
description: A use of uninitialized memory vulnerability in the pybddisasm Python bindings affects nd_to_text. If the underlying text conversion fails, including failures caused by invalid parameters, the output buffer may remain uninitialized while still being converted into a Python return value. This may disclose residual process memory or cause the Python process to crash. Exploitation requires an application to invoke nd_to_text in a way that causes conversion to fail and to return or otherwise use the resulting output. The pybddisasm package is no longer maintained.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

pid_namespace: make zap_pid_ns_processes() freezabl...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

pid_namespace: make zap_pid_ns_processes() freezable

When the init of a pid namespace exits, zap_pid_ns_processes() waits
until all other pids in the namespace are freed. A tracer outside the
namespace that does not reap its traced zombies keeps those pids
allocated, so this wait has no upper bound, and while it lasts every
suspend attempt fails:

  Freezing user space processes failed after 20.006 seconds (2 tasks refusing to freeze, wq_busy=0):

Neither wait is freezable. The first loop sleeps in do_wait(), which
returns -ERESTARTSYS on the freezer's fake signal; the loop then clears
TIF_SIGPENDING and waits again without ever freezing. The final loop
sleeps in TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE, and since nothing clears TIF_SIGPENDING
there, schedule() returns immediately after the first freeze attempt
and the task spins until the wait ends.

Sleep in TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE | TASK_FREEZABLE in do_wait(), so that the
freezer can freeze tasks waiting there directly, and in TASK_IDLE |
TASK_FREEZABLE in the final loop, like coredump_task_exit() does.

This was hit with Chromium-based browsers: crashpad ptrace-attaches the
threads of a crashed renderer, which is a pid namespace init, and does
not reap those killed during the dump.

title: Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability in Alosuite due to insufficient authorization checks when processing object...
description: Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability in Alosuite due to insufficient authorization checks when processing object identifiers. By modifying the identifier provided to the ‘/Companies/Edit/{id}’ endpoint, an attacker can access information associated with other companies or users without the appropriate authorization. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote attackers to enumerate valid object identifiers and retrieve information that should be restricted to authorized users, resulting in the unauthorized disclosure of application data.

title: Vulnerability due to a lack of request limits in Alosuite’s password recovery functionality. The ‘/Account/resetPwd’ end...
description: Vulnerability due to a lack of request limits in Alosuite’s password recovery functionality. The ‘/Account/resetPwd’ endpoint does not enforce adequate restrictions on the number or frequency of password reset requests sent for a single account. As a result, a remote attacker can repeatedly call the endpoint to generate an unlimited number of password reset emails addressed to a user, causing an email flood and enabling abuse of the password recovery mechanism. The absence of request limits or other controls against automation can harm legitimate users, consume application and email infrastructure resources, and facilitate automated attacks against the password recovery service.

title: A stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Alosuite that affects the delivery note functionality. Insufficient...
description:
A stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Alosuite that affects the delivery note functionality. Insufficient sanitization and encoding of the specified fields allow JavaScript to be stored, which executes in other users’ browsers when they view the affected records. Exploitation requires authenticated access to the affected functionality. The code can alter the displayed content and perform actions within the context of the victim’s session. The list of features, parameters, and endpoints is as follows:

CVE-2026-108050: ReferenceOtherParty in ‘/Documents/DeliveryNotes/Edit/{id}’;

title: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts vulnerability in team-alembic ash_authentication allows an una...
description:
Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts vulnerability in team-alembic ash_authentication allows an unauthenticated attacker to guess passwords and one-time passwords without limit.

The password, magic link and OTP strategies enforce brute_force_strategy by adding a preparation only to the actions they generate. When the resource defines one of those actions itself, the strategy uses it as written and nothing checked that it carried the preparation, so the setting compiled and applied no limit. The generators produce exactly this: mix ash_authentication.install writes sign_in_with_password, request_password_reset_token and request_magic_link, mix ash_authentication.upgrade then adds brute_force_strategy to those strategies, and mix ash_authentication.add_strategy.otp writes its OTP actions without the preparation. Separately, with registration_enabled? true the OTP sign-in is a create action, which preparations do not run on, so brute_force_strategy {:preparation, module} never applied to it.

This issue affects ash_authentication: from 5.0.0-rc.4 before 5.0.0-rc.16.

title:
Improper Authorization vulnerability in Apache ZooKeeper.

When SASL authentication is enabled on the client port, the s...
description:
Improper Authorization vulnerability in Apache ZooKeeper.

When SASL authentication is enabled on the client port, the server's SASL callback handler grants every authorization identity (authzid) that a client requests, without checking it against the principal the client authenticated as. The server then tries to replace the requested identity with a canonical form of the authenticated principal, derived from the zookeeper.security.auth_to_local rules. If no rule applies to the principal, canonicalization fails and the error is only logged. The client-requested authzid then becomes the session's SASL identity for all ACL checks.

An authenticated client whose principal is not covered by the auth_to_local rules can therefore claim any SASL identity. With the default rules, this includes any Kerberos principal from a realm other than the server's default realm, such as a principal from a cross-realm trusted realm. The client then gets the permissions granted to that identity in sasl ACLs. If the requested identity matches a configured zookeeper.superUser, it gets superuser access to the whole data tree.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.8.8 or 3.9.7, which fixes the issue.

title: Cocos AI is a confidential computing system for AI. In version 0.8.2 and earlier, Cocos AI accepts trusted execution env...
description: Cocos AI is a confidential computing system for AI. In version 0.8.2 and earlier, Cocos AI accepts trusted execution environment attestation Evidence when firmware patch levels and software measurements match, without binding the Evidence to an allowed platform owner or unique machine identity and without enforcing revocation. A remote attacker who controls or compromises another platform trusted by the same verifier can substitute valid Evidence from that platform and cause authorization of the wrong platform. This vulnerability is addressed in 0.9.0. However, this vulnerability can't be patched in source code alone, since the vulnerability arises from the confidential computing threat model itself.

title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in ninenines cowboy allows an unauthenticated remote ...
description:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in ninenines cowboy allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust connection process memory over HTTP/1.1.

Once a request has been received in full and its handler is still running, cowboy_http:parse/2 in src/cowboy_http.erl appends every further byte that arrives on the keep-alive connection to the connection buffer and returns to the receive loop without parsing it. The socket stays in active mode and no limit applies to this buffer: max_request_line_length, max_headers and the other parser limits only take effect once the handler returns and parsing resumes, and the only timer in this state is idle_timeout (default 60 seconds), which is reset on every received chunk. A client can therefore send an arbitrary amount of data on one connection for as long as the handler runs, and a few connections to an endpoint that holds requests open can drive the Erlang VM into out-of-memory conditions.

This issue affects cowboy: from 2.18.0 before 2.21.0.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: defer connection scavenging while session lo...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: defer connection scavenging while session locks are busy

The expiration worker holds conn_list_lock for reading while checking
for authenticated sessions. Without this change, the check can wait for
conn->session_lock or sessions_table_lock.

In destroy_previous_session(), the status updates after
ksmbd_conn_wait_idle_sess() run with both session locks held for
writing. Both the KSMBD_SESS_GOOD error path and the
KSMBD_SESS_NEED_SETUP success path call ksmbd_all_conn_set_status(),
which takes conn_list_lock for reading.

A writer queued on conn_list_lock can block these new read acquisitions.
The worker then waits for a session lock held by
destroy_previous_session(), which waits behind the writer. The writer
cannot proceed until the worker releases conn_list_lock.

Try both session locks instead of waiting in the scavenging check. Keep
the connection when either lock is busy and let the periodic worker
retry later.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: sch_teql: fix use-after-free on lower qd...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: sch_teql: fix use-after-free on lower qdisc drop

The issue: teql_master_xmit() tests the slave's ndo_start_xmit() return
value against NETDEV_TX_OK alone. A slave that consumes the skb but
returns an error code (rc < NET_XMIT_MASK, e.g. NET_XMIT_DROP) is treated
as if the skb were still owned, so the loop restores skb->dev and calls
__skb_pull() on it. A VLAN slave returns the result of dev_queue_xmit()
from its ndo_start_xmit() (propagated since cbbef5e18307), and when the
lower qdisc drops the packet that value is NET_XMIT_DROP after the skb
has been freed, giving a use-after-free in teql_master_xmit().

The Fix: test for consumption with dev_xmit_complete(), which accepts
NETDEV_TX_OK and every rc < NET_XMIT_MASK, matching other callers that
need to distinguish consumed results from busy. Only NETDEV_TX_OK keeps
the packet counted in tx_packets/tx_bytes and advances the slave; a
consumed result that is neither a success nor NET_XMIT_CN ends the
attempt and is charged to tx_dropped, so lower-qdisc drops are no longer
reported as good transmits. NET_XMIT_CN is counted like success because
it can accompany acceptance of the current packet: pfifo_head_drop drops
the old head, enqueues the current skb and returns NET_XMIT_CN.

Conditions to recreate the bug:
With CONFIG_NET_SCH_TEQL,
CONFIG_VLAN_8021Q and CONFIG_DUMMY enabled, add lkrdummy0 (dummy) and
lkrvlan0 (VLAN id 37 on lkrdummy0); set a pfifo limit 0 root on lkrdummy0
and a teql0 root on lkrvlan0; bring teql0 up with an address and send one
UDP packet to it. The VLAN xmit returns NET_XMIT_DROP from the lower
qdisc while holding a freed skb.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix fiemap wild read on empty truncate...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix fiemap wild read on empty truncated response

smb3_fiemap() treats -E2BIG from SMB2_ioctl() as a truncated range blob
and loops for the next chunk. If the server reports
STATUS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW with OutputCount == 0, SMB2_ioctl() returns
-E2BIG with out_data == NULL and out_data_len == 0, and the existing
length checks accept the empty result. The loop then evaluates

	next = out_data[num - 1].file_offset + ...

with num == 0, reading 16 bytes before NULL.

Reject a truncated range blob that contains no range, so the resume
offset is never computed from an empty response. Also require the last
range in a truncated blob to advance the resume offset without
overflowing, and to stay within the requested range; a malicious or
broken server could otherwise make no progress or underflow len and loop
forever. Free the previous response buffer before retrying.

Reproduced on 6.6.87.2 with a malicious SMB2 server that answers
FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES with STATUS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW and
OutputCount == 0; an FS_IOC_FIEMAP ioctl on the mount oopses in
cifs_fiemap() with CR2 = fffffffffffffff8. The code path is unchanged
on mainline.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: propagate shared-frag marker in skb_ze...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: propagate shared-frag marker in skb_zerocopy()

skb_zerocopy() moves frag descriptors from @from into @to and takes a
reference on each frag, but it does not copy skb_shinfo(from)->flags into
skb_shinfo(to)->flags.  A destination skb holding the same page-cache
backed frags as the source therefore reports skb_has_shared_frag() as
false.

That breaks the invariant relied on by later in-place writers.  ESP input
checks skb_has_shared_frag() before deciding whether an uncloned
nonlinear skb can skip skb_cow_data(); with the marker lost, an skb that
skb_zerocopy() built for nfnetlink_queue or for an openvswitch upcall is
decrypted in place, letting an unprivileged user write into the page
cache of a root-owned read-only file.

Propagate SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when frag descriptors are copied, as done for
the other frag-transfer helpers.

title: Missing Authorization vulnerability in the device and deployment group pages in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an auth...
description:
Missing Authorization vulnerability in the device and deployment group pages in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated organization member with the view role to change devices and deployment groups via LiveView events reserved for the manage role. The event handlers that add and delete device certificates, add and remove tags, overwrite or clear a device's manual location, remove a device from its deployment group, move matched devices into a deployment group or remove unmatched ones, import devices from a CSV, and start, retry or delete firmware delta builds carry out the change without calling authorized!/2, and the pages render the controls to every member.

A view member can add a certificate that lets whoever holds its key connect as the device, delete a certificate so the device can no longer authenticate with it, and change which deployment group, and so which firmware release, a device receives. Everything stays within the organizations the member belongs to.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

title: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in the devices page bulk move in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated...
description:
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in the devices page bulk move in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated user with the manage role in one organization and only the view role in another to move devices into the second organization's product via the "Move device(s) to product" action. The target-product event in NervesHubWeb.Live.Devices.Index looks the product up with NervesHub.Products.get_by_id/2, which checks that the user is a member of the product's organization at any role, and move-devices-product then changes each selected device's organization and product. The device API's move requires manage in the target organization, and an earlier fix added the check on the organization the devices leave but not on the one they enter.

A moved device keeps its key and certificate, joins the target organization's matching deployment groups, and is sent their firmware with a download URL, which the view role cannot otherwise obtain. The user cannot change or control devices that already belong to the other organization.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

title: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes vulnerability in the device API, device f...
description:
Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes vulnerability in the device API, device forms, signing key and product forms and JITP settings in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated user who manages devices in any organization to write into other organizations via submitted org_id, product_id and deployment_id fields. The device API create and update actions and the dashboard device forms pass the request parameters to NervesHub.Devices.Device.changeset/2, which casts the organization, product, deployment group and update state as given. The signing key and product forms merge the session's organization into the submitted parameters so that a submitted org_id wins, and the JITP changeset accepts any product_id. Each request requires the manage role only in the user's own organization, and any account can create one.

A device placed on another organization's deployment group, or moved into its product, is sent that organization's firmware with a download URL. The user cannot change or control devices that already belong to the other organization, and cannot upload firmware to it.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

The potential vulnerability may impact the confidentiality (high), integrity (high) and availability (high) of the vulnerable system, resulting in subsequent system confidentiality (high), integrity (high) and availability (high) impacts.

title: When a CalDAV or ICS calendar was accessed through an HTTP proxy that requested authentication, Thunderbird could answer...
description: When a CalDAV or ICS calendar was accessed through an HTTP proxy that requested authentication, Thunderbird could answer the proxy with the calendar server's username and password. This affected both setting up a new calendar and syncing existing calendars, where a saved password could be sent without any user interaction. A malicious or compromised proxy could use this to obtain the calendar credentials, even for calendars served over HTTPS. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 160 and Thunderbird 153.7.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: nft_byteorder: remove multi-register sup...
description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: nft_byteorder: remove multi-register support

64bit byteorder conversion is broken when several registers need to be
converted because the source register array advances in steps for 4 bytes
instead of 8:

  for (i = ...
      src64 = nft_reg_load64(&src[i]);
                             ~~~~~ u32 *src
      nft_reg_store64(&dst64[i],

Remove the multi-register support, it has other issues as well:

Pablo points out that commit
caf3ef7468f7 ("netfilter: nf_tables: prevent OOB access in nft_byteorder_eval")
alters semantics: before the loop operated on registers, i.e.
 for ( ... )
   dst32[i] = htons((u16)src32[i])

 .. but after the patch it will operate on bytes, which makes this
 useless to convert e.g. concatenations, which store each compound
 in its own register.

Multi-convert of u32 has one theoretical application:

ct mark . meta mark . tcp dport @intervalset

Because ct mark and meta mark are host byte order, use with
intervals has to convert the byteorder for ct/meta mark value
to network byte order (bigendian).

nftables emits this:
 [ meta load mark => reg 1 ]
 [ byteorder reg 1 = hton(reg 1, 4, 4) ]
 [ ct load mark => reg 9 ]
 [ byteorder reg 9 = hton(reg 9, 4, 4) ]
 ...

I.e. two separate calls.  Theoretically it could be changed to do:
 [ meta load mark => reg 1 ]
 [ ct load mark => reg 9 ]
 [ byteorder reg 1 = htonl(reg 1, 4, 8) ]
 ...

But then all it would take to change the set to
meta mark . tcp dport . ct mark

... and we'd be back to two "byteorder" calls. IOW, support to
convert a range of registers is both dysfunctional and dubious.

Simplify this: remove the feature.

Pablo Neira Ayuso points out that nftables before 1.1.0 can generate
incorrect byteorder conversions, see 9fe58952c45a,
"evaluate: skip byteorder conversion for selector smaller than 2 bytes"
in nftables.git).  Affected rulesets fail to load with this change and
old userspace due to 'len != size' check.

title: When a message was forwarded inline, edited as new, or had an attachment dragged into a compose window, a specially craf...
description:
When a message was forwarded inline, edited as new, or had an attachment dragged into a compose window, a specially crafted link attachment (a .desktop file on Linux, or a .url or .lnk file on Windows) was replaced with the content of the file or URL it pointed to when the message was saved or sent. This could disclose local files, or content from the user's network, to the message recipients or to the mail provider.
This bug only affects Thunderbird on Linux and Windows. Other operating systems are unaffected. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 160 and Thunderbird 153.7.

Thunderbird allowed feed subscriptions to file: URLs that point to a network share. If a user was tricked into subscribing to such a URL, Thunderbird connected to the attacker's server when fetching the feed. Windows then sent the user's NTLM credentials to that server.
This bug only affects Thunderbird on Windows. Other operating systems are unaffected. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 160 and Thunderbird 153.7.

title: Rooxis RXR-12 Wi-Fi router contains an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in /usr/bin/cloud_manage, whe...
description: Rooxis RXR-12 Wi-Fi router contains an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in /usr/bin/cloud_manage, where a server-controlled JSON diagnoseParameter field is passed unsanitized to popen(), enabling arbitrary command execution as root over cleartext HTTP when an attacker is positioned on-path and has access to the hard-coded cloud endpoint. Firmware 20260813_c2169ea5 fixes the vulnerability, and your router can be updated through the local web interface.

title: Rooxis RXR-12 Wi-Fi router contains an authenticated command injection vulnerability in the LuCI white_list RPC handler ...
description: Rooxis RXR-12 Wi-Fi router contains an authenticated command injection vulnerability in the LuCI white_list RPC handler (/usr/lib/lua/luci/data/white_list_plt.lua), where unsanitized user-supplied MAC addresses are concatenated into os.execute() without validation, yielding root command execution via a malformed mac parameter. Firmware 20260813_c2169ea5 fixes the vulnerability, and users can update their router through the local web interface.

title: Missing Authorization vulnerability in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows a weblog member with the Limited role to r...
description:
Missing Authorization vulnerability in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows a weblog member with the Limited role to remove or change entries that member may only read, including entries published by other members. The entry editor checked the member's weblog role but not whether that role permits work on the entry.
Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later.

title: repmgr 4.0.0 through 5.5.0 is affected by an OS command injection vulnerability (CWE-78) in event notifications. When ev...
description: repmgr 4.0.0 through 5.5.0 is affected by an OS command injection vulnerability (CWE-78) in event notifications. When event_notification_command is configured, repmgr substitutes the %a (node name), %c (connection string) and %d (details) placeholders into the command and runs it through the shell. %a and %c are inserted without escaping, and %d escapes only double quotes, so shell command substitution still works inside the quoting the documentation recommends. The node name and connection string come from node records in the repmgr.nodes table. An attacker with the credentials of a non-superuser repmgr database user can write a crafted node record and run OS commands, as the operating system user that runs repmgr or repmgrd (usually postgres), on other cluster nodes that process an event using these placeholders. The %a placeholder of failover_validation_command has the same flaw. Deployments whose repmgr database user is a superuser gain no new capability, because a superuser can already run OS commands, and deployments that do not use these placeholders are not affected. The issue is fixed in repmgr 5.5.1. After upgrading, operators must remove any quotes they placed around these placeholders, because a placeholder left inside double quotes is still open to command injection.

title: This vulnerability exists in the eMudhra emBridge due to missing authorization checks in the FileBrowser API endpoints. ...
description:
This vulnerability exists in the eMudhra emBridge due to missing authorization checks in the FileBrowser API endpoints. These endpoints perform file system enumeration using the LocalSystem account without adequately validating the requesting caller's authorization. An unauthenticated attacker on the same LAN could exploit this vulnerability by sending malicious webpage to the local HTTPS Web API.

 

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to enumerate file and directory names and obtain information about the directory structure of the targeted system. 



The vulnerability however, does not provide access to file contents or permit file modification, deletion, or code execution, or access to cryptographic keys and hardware token PINs.

title: Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the PATCH /api/user/files/:id rename endpoint that allo...
description: Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the PATCH /api/user/files/:id rename endpoint that allows authenticated users to overwrite existing uploads by supplying unsanitized names. Attackers can submit names like ../uploads/victim.txt that bypass the raw-string database uniqueness check but normalize via path.join(), causing fs.rename() to replace other files' contents.

title: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server allows a client to stall a...
description:
Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server allows a client to stall all later calls on a shared HTTP/2 connection via calls that the server refuses while their DATA frames are in flight.

The stream handler grpc_stream_h (grpc_server/src/grpc_stream_h.erl) requests flow from Cowboy only for request data that has arrived. When the server refuses a call early, for example because the body exceeds max_body_size or the method is not implemented, Cowboy drops the DATA frames still in flight for that stream. Their bytes are not returned to the connection flow-control window. After enough refused calls the window is empty. No call on that connection can then send a request body, and each call waits until its deadline. Other connections are not affected.

This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server and grpc allows an attacker to...
description:
Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server and grpc allows an attacker to make a handler act on a resource other than the one named in the URL of an HTTP-transcoded route, via a request with a gRPC Content-Type.

Only the transcoding clause of GRPC.Server.do_handle_request/4 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server.ex, and lib/grpc/server.ex before the package split) applies the route's path bindings to the request message. The Cowboy handler picks that clause from the request Content-Type, not from the route. A request to a transcoded URL with application/grpc or application/grpc-web is decoded from the body alone, so every path-bound field takes its value from the body. A gateway, proxy rule or WAF that authorizes on the URL path sees one resource while the handler receives another.

This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0; grpc: from 0.8.0 before 1.0.0.

title:
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



An authenticated user who holds any one of a route's required...
description:
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



An authenticated user who holds any one of a route's required permissions or scopes can reach the protected upstream without the others, including HTTP methods the authorization server denied.



This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 1.4.0 through 3.19.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.
